questions.question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose ‘No improvement’ as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

Raccoons __have being more__ active at night.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Option 1: **are more'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The underlined part of the sentence contains an error in the verb tense. The 'present progressive' tense, indicated by** 'have being'** is **incorrect** in this context.
 
• The **sentence talks about **a habitual behavior of raccoons. Thus, a simple present tense should be used to indicate an action that is generally true, happens often, or is a fact.
 
• **By replacing** **'have being'** with **'are',** we can create a grammatically correct sentence: "Raccoons are more active at night."
 
• This sentence effectively communicates that generally, or as a fact, raccoons show increased activity during the night.

Therefore, the** correct answer** is- 'Option 1:** are more'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Option 2 **'are few'** is incorrect as it changes the meaning of the sentence and does not make grammatical sense.
 
• Option 4** 'are much'** is incorrect as 'much' typically quantifies uncountable nouns and does not fit in this sentence.

questions.question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.

Professor Murli's eyebrows / rose a little higher and his / gaze became distinctly coldest.

options.text: rose a little higher and his

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 1'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** error in the** sentence is in the phrase "gaze became distinctly coldest". 
 
• **In English,** we** don't often use** the superlative form ("coldest") with "distinctly" or any other adverbs of degree. It **would be more appropriate** to say "gaze became distinctly cold" or "became the coldest", without the adverb.
 
• **In the correct** form, "gaze became distinctly cold", the adverb "distinctly" modifies the adjective "cold", intensifying the degree to which his gaze became cold.
 
• In the other form, "gaze became the coldest", "the coldest" is a superlative adjective, showing that his gaze is at the highest degree of coldness, compared to other references (if any) in the given context.

Therefore, the** corrected sentence would be**:* "Professor Murli's eyebrows rose a little higher and his gaze became distinctly cold" or "gaze became the coldest".*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **"Professor Murli's eyebrows"** **(Option 3)**: This segment of the sentence contains no grammatical error. It is grammatically correct to refer to a person’s physical features in this way.
 
• **"rose a little higher and his" (Option 4)**: This segment is also grammatically correct. It means Professor Murli's eyebrows moved upwards to a slightly greater height, which is often a sign of surprise or disbelief.

questions.question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

Without the greenhouse effect, Earths temperature would be below freezing.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Option 1: **Earths temperature would'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence uses an incorrect form of the noun **'Earth'. **
 
• **It should** be** 'Earth's'** rather than 'Earths' as the phrase 'Earths temperature' signifies temperature belonging to the Earth, demanding possessive form 'Earth's'.
 
• **The erroneous part** of the sentence, "Earths temperature would," should instead be "Earth's temperature would."
 
• This corrected sentence effectively communicates the possible condition if there was no greenhouse effect.

The **corrected sentence** reads: *"Without the greenhouse effect, Earth's temperature would be below freezing."*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2 **'be below freezing.' is correct as it stands and does not require any modification. The phrase denotes the state of temperature without the greenhouse effect.
 
• **Option 3** 'Without the greenhouse effect,' is also grammatically correct, emphasizing the situation in the absence of the greenhouse effect.

questions.question:
Select the word segment that substitutes (replaces) the bracketed word segment correctly and completes the sentence meaningfully. Select the option 'no correction required' if the sentence is correct as given.

With a (sudden push off understanding), Harry realised who the people in the end beds must be.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Option 1' i.e.** 'Sudden rush of understanding'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error in the sentence lies in the phrase** "sudden push off understanding"**. This phrase appears awkward and doesn't adhere to conventional English syntax and semantics.
 
• **The correct phrase** to indicate a sudden realization or epiphany is "sudden rush of understanding," which suggests that understanding has arrived quickly and intensely.
 
• This means Harry quickly understood or comprehended the identities of the people in the end beds.

Therefore, the **corrected sentence** would be: *"With a sudden rush of understanding, Harry realised who the people in the end beds must be".*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• "suddenly rushed understanding" **(Option 2)**: This phrase does not convey the correct meaning. One cannot have a "rushed understanding." Understanding is something that comes to a person rather than being rushed. The phrase is grammatically incorrect and awkward.
 
• "all of sudden understand" **(Option 4):** This option is grammatically incorrect and does not carry the same meaning as the correct answer. A possible correction could be "all of a sudden, understood" but still, the phrase "sudden rush of understanding" is more precise and suitable in this context.

questions.question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

All work and __none play__ makes Jack a dull boy.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 1' **i.e. **'No play'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error in the sentence can be found in the phrase** "none play".** This phrase is grammatically incorrect in this context.
 
• This sentence is actually a well-known proverb that uses a specific grammatical structure, and the correct form should be** "no play".** The proverb means that without taking time off from work to relax and have fun, a person becomes bored and boring.
 
• Therefore, the **corrected sentence **would be: "All work and no play makes Jack a dull boy".
 
• This sentence highlights the importance of balance in life, namely that constant working without any leisure or recreation can lead to dullness or lack of creativity.

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is:* **"All work and no play makes Jack a dull boy".*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• "None plays"** (Option 3): **The use of "plays" after "none" is grammatically incorrect in this context as this does not fit the intended meaning of the sentence.
 
• "No played"** (Option 4): **"Played" is the past tense of the verb "play". In the given sentence, we need the noun form "play" to represent the idea of recreation or leisure activity, not the past tense of the verb, making this option incorrect.

• The term** 'Breathable'** is a perfect fit here. It refers to material that allows air to circulate freely, thus making the wear more comfortable in a warm environment.
 
• The sentence therefore reads: "Since the temperatures can soar in summer, choose clothing that is lightweight and breathable."
 
• This sentence effectively gives guidance on what clothing is suitable during hot weather.

Therefore, the** correct answer** is- **'Breathable'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Option 4:** 'Hefty'**, meaning large and heavy, is again not suitable for the context where lightweight clothing is preferred.

questions.question:
A sentence has been given with a blank to be filled with an appropriate option. Choose the correct alternative.

__________ every nation in the world is now administering vaccines.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Option 1' i.e.** 'Nearly'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In this sentence, **we need an adverb** to modify the verb phrase "is now administering vaccines." The **adverb should indicate** the extent to which the nations are administering vaccines.
 
• The term **"nearly"** is an adverb meaning almost all or most. It is the correct word to complete the sentence because it signifies that almost every nation is administering vaccines.
 
• Therefore, the completed sentence is: "Nearly every nation in the world is now administering vaccines."
 
• This sentence asserts that almost every nation worldwide is now involved in the process of administering vaccines, likely in response to a health concern or pandemic.

Therefore, the** correct sentence** is: *'Nearly every nation in the world is now administering vaccines.'*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **"Near" (Option 2)**: "Near" is a preposition, adjective, or adverb, but it doesn't work in this context because it indicates proximity in space or time, not extensive action or a high numerical count.
 
• **"Nearest" (Option 3)**: This word is the superlative form of "near" and is used to indicate the closest in degree, amount, or space. It's not applicable in this context because we need an adverb to indicate the vast number of nations, not proximity.
 
• **"Nearer" (Option 4):** "Nearer" is the comparative form of "near," which indicates lesser distance or correlation. It does not fit the meaning required in this context.
